title: Hot weather in the UK is now almost as deadly as a cold snap | New Scientist
description: Cold weather has always killed more people than hot weather in England and Wales – that's about to change
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: Workout patch delivers some of the benefits of exercise with no exertion | New Scientist
description: Injecting muscle cells beneath the skin of mice led to a patch of self-contracting cells that boosted their muscle mass, bone density and even markers of good brain, immune and liver function
author: Chris Simms

title: Shingles vaccine may lower risk of stroke and heart failure | New Scientist
description: Being vaccinated against shingles has been linked to a lower risk of cardiovascular disease before, but now a study suggests that the vaccine that is currently being used reduces the odds more than earlier versions of the shot
author: Carissa Wong

title: Lack of sleep may cause anxiety by making us less adaptable to threats | New Scientist
description: People who were deprived of sleep overnight didn't seem to adapt to being in a potentially threatening space, which may help explain the link between a lack of shuteye and anxiety
author: Tosin Thompson

title: Risk of dementia could be halved with use of metformin | New Scientist
description: Taking metformin, a type 2 diabetes drug, has been linked to a lower risk of dementia over the following decades, but the association isn't conclusive
author: Michael Marshall

title: Dice discovered that solve decade-long mathematical problem | New Scientist
description: After years of searching, mathematicians have found dice that can allow five players to fairly decide who moves first in a board game, with a winner guaranteed from just a single roll
author: Matthew Sparkes
